name: 35 mm f/1.8 mirrorless-native wide-angle prime (patent numerical example)
representativeSource: Three independent sources agree. (1) photonstophotos.net Optical Bench Hub's model list ties patent JP2019-090947, Example04P, to "Nikon Nikkor Z 35mm f/1.8 S" (https://www.photonstophotos.net/GeneralTopics/Lenses/OpticalBench/OpticalBenchHub.htm, accessed 9/28/2026; row in .local/lens-normal/modeldata.tsv). (2) The Hub's own per-lens data file, https://www.photonstophotos.net/GeneralTopics/Lenses/OpticalBench/Data/JP2019-090947_Example04P.txt (accessed 9/28/2026, William J. Claff), titles this exact example "JP 2019-090947 Example 4 (Nikon Nikkor Z 35mm f/1.8 S)", cites the figure source as Nikon's own Asia product page (nikon-asia.com/.../nikkor-z-35mm-f-1-8-s.html), and independently transcribes the same 23-surface prescription - his scaled r/nd/vd/asph values match this file's raw values times scale=22.5 exactly, to the last printed digit, confirming the transcription. His notes also independently flag the identical total-length gap this workstream found ("Sum d = 4.40 but TL is 4.553") and diagnose the same fix ("Surface 5 d 0.108 -> 0.261"), which is applied here (see notes) and closes both the TL gap and the EFL/BF self-check to within tolerance - strong evidence the correction is real and not a coincidence. (3) asobinet.com (Japanese lens-patent blog), https://asobinet.com/info-patent-nikkor-z-35mm-nikon-minolta/, accessed 9/28/2026, separately identifies the same Nikon/Konica Minolta joint patent family (JP2019-090947/090948/090949, all filed 11/15/2017, published 6/13/2019) as the source of the Z 35mm f/1.8 S design, citing the identical numbers (f=1.57, FNO=1.85, TL=4.553, BF=0.0425) for what it labels "Example 3" of sibling application JP2019-090949 - the same raw prescription transcribed here as Example 4 of JP2019-090947. Corroborated structurally, decisively, by a fourth, independent check: this transcription's element/group count from the engine's own cemented-interface rule is 11 elements in 9 groups, matching Nikon's own published "11 elements in 9 groups" exactly (nikonusa.com) and confirmed by this project's own vitest assertions; 3 of those 11 elements carry aspheric surfaces (patent surfaces 11-12, 18-19, 20-21, each biaspheric), matching Nikon's published "3 aspherical elements" exactly; and the two highest-Abbe-number elements (patent surface 9, nd=1.49700/vd=81.61; patent surface 16, nd=1.59282/vd=68.62) are consistent with Nikon's published "2 ED glass elements", though no source ties those two specific surfaces to a named ED glass product by name, so that last piece is circumstantial, not confirmed. The design's genuinely small back focus (about 0.96-0.98 mm at real scale) is corroborated independently by Claff's own "Bf(p)"/"Bf" fields (0.95625 / 0.97), not an artifact of this workstream's own scale choice.

Nikon's shipped minimum focus distance (0.25 m, see focus.minFocusM) is not derived from this patent value; the two need not agree because the patent's own close-focus example is not necessarily the shipped lens's closest point (same situation documented in m50.json's minFocusSource note).

notes: Source is Nikon/Konica Minolta's joint JP2019-090947A ("Image capturing lens, image capturing optical device, and digital equipment" / 撮像レンズ、撮像光学装置及びデジタル機器), application JP2017-220250, filed 11/15/2017, published 6/13/2019, granted as JP7015679B2. The same filing produced sibling applications JP2019-090948A and JP2019-090949A on the same day (per asobinet.com, a Japanese lens-patent blog); this file transcribes JP2019-090947A's own Example 4, whose numbers (f=1.57, FNO=1.85, TL=4.553, BF=0.0425) are the SAME numbers asobinet.com quotes for "Example 3" of sibling JP2019-090949A, so the three co-filed applications evidently share overlapping numerical examples under different example numbers; JP2019-090949A itself was not separately fetched or transcribed here.

SCALE NOTE: this patent's own surface-data table is normalized to a tiny unit system (stated focal length f=1.57 'mm', total length 4.553 'mm', BF=0.0425 'mm', close-focus object distance 7.0 'mm') that is far too small to be the lens's real physical size despite the patent's literal 'mm' labels - the patent's own background section describes 'a compact, wide-angle, large-aperture imaging lens suitable for a lens-interchangeable digital camera', which is inconsistent with a 4.553 mm-long, 1.57 mm-focal-length physical lens. This is standard practice for this kind of lens-design patent: the printed table is a normalized reference prescription, and any absolute physical size sharing the same radius/thickness ratios is claimed. `scale` = 22.5 is William J. Claff's own value (photonstophotos.net Optical Bench Hub data file for this exact example; see representativeSource), not independently re-derived here; it scales the design's raw stated focal length (1.57) to 35.325 mm, not to an exactly-round 35.000 mm, which is consistent with how every other lens file in this project keeps `focalLength` as the nominal marketed class while `stated.f` (and here, the scaled real f) can differ from it slightly (e.g. p35.json's raw f=36.00 for its nominal 35mm class). This workstream did not determine independently how Claff derived 22.5 specifically (plausibly by matching the design's own image circle to the real Z-mount FX sensor diagonal, 43.2 mm, which his data file lists as an exact round number - a more principled anchor than this workstream's earlier, since-replaced assumption of scaling to a round 35.000mm nominal focal length), but adopting his figure is justified because it is what makes the design's own paraxial EFL/BF self-check close (see the self-check note below) - i.e. it is corroborated by physics, not merely borrowed on authority.

Element/group count: this schema's engine (src/engine/lens.ts) counts consecutive glass surfaces joined with no air gap as separate cemented elements sharing one group (same rule documented in m50.json's notes). Applying that rule here: patent surfaces 3-4 are a cemented doublet (2 elements, 1 group), 6-7 are a cemented doublet (2 elements, 1 group), and surfaces 1, 9, 11-12 (biaspheric singlet), 14, 16, 18-19 (biaspheric singlet), 20-21 (biaspheric singlet) are each one singlet element/group. Total: 1 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 11 elements in 9 groups, matching Nikon's own published '11 elements in 9 groups' spec exactly (nikonusa.com) - this is the strongest structural confirmation that this patent example is the Z 35mm f/1.8 S design, independent of the photonstophotos.net/asobinet.com ties.

TRANSCRIPTION CORRECTION (resolved): the patent's own printed/OCR'd surface-5 thickness (d5) reads 0.108 in both the English machine translation and the embedded Japanese original of JP2019-090947A - confirmed twice against both renderings, so it is not a translation artifact - but summing all 23 raw thicknesses with d5=0.108 gives total length 4.4015, not the patent's own stated TL=4.553 (a 3.4% gap), and the same raw data fails the required paraxial EFL/BF self-check by 3.4%/46%. William J. Claff's independent transcription of this exact example (photonstophotos.net Optical Bench Hub data file, see representativeSource) carries the same discrepancy in his own working notes ("Sum d = 4.40 but TL is 4.553") and the same diagnosis ("Surface 5 d 0.108 -> 0.261"). Substituting d5=0.261 (this file's current value) closes the total-length sum to 4.5545 (vs. stated 4.553, off by 0.03%) and brings the required self-check to EFL +0.153% and BFD +0.026 mm (both within tolerance; see research/lenses-z35.md). Two independent researchers reaching the same specific fix from the same specific symptom is strong evidence 0.108 is a genuine misprint/OCR error in the patent's own published table (most likely '0.108' for what should print as '0.261' - not obviously a single-character OCR slip, so possibly an error already present in the patent office's own typesetting) and 0.261 is correct; this is the one number in this file that is NOT the patent's own printed value.

Aspheric K convention is NOT confirmed independently for this patent. Unlike p24/p28/p35/m50 (where the patent text was found to explicitly state 'K=0 means a sphere' or an equivalent kappa relation), no such defining sentence was found in this patent's machine-translated text for its own aspheric-data block. K is therefore stored as printed (k = K, not k = K-1) by default/convention-of-least-assumption; this matters only for the aspheric shape at high ray heights (second-order and beyond), not for the paraxial EFL/BF self-check, which ignores all aspheric terms by construction (same as every other lens file in this project). Flagged for whichever workstream builds the real (non-paraxial) ray tracer to confirm against rendered spot diagrams.

Semi-diameters ARE patent-stated for every surface (column 'Ri' in the [Surface data] table, and 'R13' in the [Variable parameter] table for the stop) - unlike p24/p28/p35/p50/m50, whose patents print no effective-diameter column at all. sdSource is 'patent' throughout this file, not 'estimated-from-marginal-ray'.
medium is 'glass' (not a catalog key) everywhere because the patent gives only nd/vd, never a named glass catalog product; same situation as every other lens file in this project.
Object-side reference point for closeObjectDistance (7.0, raw/pre-scale) is not stated in the translated text, same caveat as every other lens file's closeObjectDistance note.

No public source independently confirms which two of this design's 11 elements are Nikon's '2 ED' elements by product glass name; the two highest-Abbe-number elements (surfaces 9 and 16, vd=81.61 and vd=68.62) are noted as circumstantially consistent, not confirmed.
